editorial.description_en: A lime-washed wall in daylight: a light neutral that reads faintly warm without turning to cream.
editorial.description_ja: 石灰をぬった壁のような、明るくおだやかな色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.878, C 0.009, h 66.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 石灰 (sekkai, lime) + 壁 (kabe, wall). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Lime Wall" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 石灰壁. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — asa-nuno at ΔE00 3.7, kawaki-suna at ΔE00 4.9, kai-jiro at ΔE00 4.9. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.009 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
